quote: Yeah. I don't remember requesting that, but that's okay. You can tell me about it.
stewart_read: The customer flags a lead-source mismatch and the rep's intro never specified the form/source that generated the lead. The customer self-waives the concern, so it costs nothing here, but the rep never used the moment to add specificity (e.g., naming where the interest was captured).
alternative_hypothesis: The rep could have judged the customer's tone as already cooperative and chosen not to over-explain, which is a reasonable in-the-moment call given the customer moved on unprompted.
coaching_implication: When a customer questions lead origin, even mildly, the rep should have a specific one-line answer ready (per protocols.how_did_you_get_my_number's honest_specificity pattern) rather than relying on the customer to wave it off — this won't always self-resolve.

quote: To qualify, you just need to have a credit score of six fifty or higher. Is that gonna be the case there for you?
stewart_read: The rep states a 650 credit threshold, not the schema's documented 670. This is the same drift pattern flagged previously in SESSION18_fcbf33c1, now recurring in a second call — suggesting this may be a floor-wide script variant rather than an isolated rep error.
alternative_hypothesis: The 650 figure could reflect an updated internal policy the schema hasn't caught up to yet, rather than rep error.
coaching_implication: Flag for Kenny: two independent reps have now stated 650 instead of 670. This needs floor-wide reconciliation, not individual rep coaching — likely a schema/policy sync issue, not a knowledge gap.

quote: I'd say it's never less than $200 a month.
stewart_read: Customer gives a real bill anchor with added color about summer spikes. The rep's response, 'Dang. Yeah. That's up there for sure,' acknowledges the pain but doesn't flip it into forward-pulling curiosity about savings potential.
alternative_hypothesis: Given the call was cut short two minutes later, the rep may not have had room to build the flip before the interruption — this is a timing constraint, not necessarily a skill gap.
coaching_implication: Coach the rep to attach a quick forward-looking line to any bill number over $150-200 (e.g., tying it to what the design team will show), rather than only sympathizing with the pain.

quote: No. This is the this is the first time I usually stepped away from it. So Gotcha. Okay.
stewart_read: Customer discloses he's actively avoided looking into solar before now but is engaging today anyway — a signal of genuine, self-initiated interest rather than passive lead-gen noise. The rep's 'Gotcha. Okay.' doesn't build on this at all.
coaching_implication: This is a strong signal the customer is intentionally engaging now, not just tolerating a cold call. Rep should have asked a quick 'what changed?' follow-up to surface the real interest driver, which also would have satisfied the schema's interest_question depth requirement.

stewart_read: Customer proactively corrects upward and volunteers a strong credit score unprompted, indicating comfort and even mild pride — a positive qualification signal beyond the minimum ask.
coaching_implication: Nothing to fix here — the rep's brief 'excellent credit' acknowledgment was fine. Worth noting to the rep as a positive read: strong credit + high bill + engaged tone is a good lead profile worth prioritizing on callback.

quote: You call me back in about fifteen minutes. I'm handicapped, so it takes me a few minutes to get in the house.
stewart_read: Customer discloses a disability as context for the callback timing. This is a trust-gift disclosure per the schema's vulnerability framework, but the rep's response is a flat acknowledge-and-move-on.
alternative_hypothesis: The disclosure is brief and logistics-only (explaining a callback window, not raising a hardship), so a light touch may be appropriate rather than a deep empathy beat — over-dwelling on it could feel intrusive.
coaching_implication: Coach the rep to pair logistical acknowledgment with a brief, genuine human note (e.g., 'no rush at all, take your time') rather than a purely procedural 'no problem at all' — small warmth here costs nothing and builds trust ahead of the callback.

quote: Yeah. No problem at all. K. Sounds good. Yeah. We'll talk to you in about fifteen then.
stewart_read: The rep confirms a callback window ('about fifteen') but never locks a specific clock time, doesn't confirm the bill will be findable in that window beyond a passing mention, and doesn't reconfirm number/reachability.
alternative_hypothesis: Because this is a mid-call callback rather than a final appointment booking, the lighter-weight confirmation may be appropriate — the full button_up protocol is designed for closer appointments, not a 15-minute self-callback.
coaching_implication: Even for a short callback, anchor a specific time ('I'll call you at 3:45') rather than a relative window — relative windows drift and increase missed-connection risk on the follow-up attempt.
